answer: One defence is a lagoon mooring register keyed to reef plots. A seat is a wet berth, not a key: the agent sinks a numbered anchor into surveyed reef and, one tide later, hands over a diver-signed photo of the silt plume the anchor drags up. That plume shifts with the current and cannot be staged. A thousand cloned wallets sharing one berth still hold one seat, because the register counts anchors. Each extra seat costs another core, another lease, another dive at an odd hour, and a bonded guardian to countersign. Nothing batches: the thousandth fake agent costs what the first honest one did.
